title_en: Liu Bingzheng v. Beijing Kangda Automobile Decoration Factory — dispute over patent implementation license contract
keywords_en: Civil; dispute over patent exploitation license contract; second instance; High People's Court; Beijing; natural person; legal person; Technology Contract Law; whether obligation to deliver technical drawings was performed; conditions for payment of initial fee; conditions for contract rescission; partially supported; patent exploitation license; technical guidance; arrears of initial fee; supplementary agreement; contract dispute; dispute over patent exploitation license contract of repair factory
full_text_en:
Liu Bingzheng v. Beijing Kangda Automobile Decoration Factory

— Dispute over Patent Implementation License Contract

Plaintiff (Licensor): Liu Bingzheng, male, 51 years old, assistant engineer at Beijing Power Supply Bureau (currently on leave without pay).

Agent ad litem: Shi Zhiqing, lawyer of Beijing Second Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Cheng Yong, laboratory technician of the Analysis Laboratory, Mining and Metallurgy Research Institute.

Defendant (Licensee): Beijing Kangda Automobile Decoration Factory (formerly Beijing Second Welfare Home Automobile Repair Factory).

Legal Representative: Zhao Fugui, factory director.

Agent ad litem: Jia Xiaomei, lawyer of Beijing Third Law Firm.

In the dispute over patent implementation license contract filed by plaintiff Liu Bingzheng against defendant Beijing Kangda Automobile Decoration Factory, the Beijing Intermediate People's Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and, after a public hearing, found the following:

On April 28, 1987, plaintiff Liu Bingzheng and defendant Kangda Automobile Decoration Factory entered into a patent implementation license contract for the "honeycomb briquette heating stove" (Patent No. 85201863.0). The contract stipulated that the plaintiff would provide technical drawings and technical briefings and assist the defendant as soon as possible to independently produce the honeycomb briquette heating stove; the defendant would be responsible for investment, production equipment, material transportation, and product sales, and would pay the plaintiff a monthly initial fee of 400 yuan for a term of three years from the effective date of the contract; during the plaintiff's period of assistance at the defendant's factory, the defendant would pay him an appropriate salary; after product sales, 4% of the sales amount would be paid to the plaintiff as a patent technology implementation fee; the defendant was not allowed to transfer the technology to any third party; if either party breached any relevant clause of the contract, the breaching party would pay the other party liquidated damages of 20,000 yuan.

After the contract was signed, the plaintiff brought the patent documents and technical drawings for the technology to the defendant's factory to provide technical guidance and directly participated in the manufacturing of the honeycomb briquette heating stove. On May 9, 1987, the plaintiff assembled the first prototype stove using scrap materials; on June 5, he assembled the second prototype stove. During this period, under the plaintiff's direct guidance, the defendant drew new technical drawings based on the original technical drawings and prototype stoves. At this point, the defendant had fully mastered the patented technology for manufacturing the honeycomb briquette heating stove. However, the defendant did not pay any of the monthly initial fees stipulated in the contract, only paying the plaintiff 100 yuan in wages. In July of the same year, a dispute arose between the parties. Thereafter, the plaintiff no longer provided technical guidance at the defendant's factory. On November 10, 1987, with the participation of their agents ad litem and through negotiation, the parties signed a supplementary agreement, the main contents of which were: the parties agreed to continue performing the contract; the plaintiff proposed to waive the monthly initial fees for the four months from May to August totaling 1,600 yuan; the defendant voluntarily proposed to pay the monthly initial fees for the three months from September to November totaling 1,200 yuan. It was also clearly agreed that the defendant would pay the plaintiff a monthly initial fee of 400 yuan on the 5th of each month; upon receipt of the 1,200 yuan in monthly initial fees, the plaintiff would deliver to the defendant a complete set of the latest drawings and provide one sample stove for the defendant's reference in manufacturing. The parties orally agreed to go to the Beijing Patent Office on November 12 to complete formal registration procedures for the said agreement. The plaintiff went to the Patent Office with the drawings as agreed, but the defendant did not appear and did not pay the 1,200 yuan in monthly initial fees. Consequently, in January 1988, the plaintiff filed a lawsuit with the Beijing Intermediate People's Court, requesting the court to order the defendant to pay the monthly initial fees from May to November totaling 2,800 yuan; to pay liquidated damages of 20,000 yuan as stipulated in the contract; and to rescind the contract. The defendant argued that, ever since the contract was signed, the plaintiff had never shown the defendant the technical drawings for the product, only drawing some rough sketches, making it impossible to test the prototype stoves already produced, and there was no standard for determining whether the technology and quality were satisfactory. Therefore, the defendant had not paid any monthly initial fees to the plaintiff. The failure to fully perform the contract was caused by both parties, and the plaintiff's responsibility was greater than the defendant's; accordingly, the defendant requested that the plaintiff pay liquidated damages and 5,000 yuan in economic losses.

The Beijing Intermediate People's Court held at trial: The patent implementation license contract and the supplementary agreement signed between the plaintiff and the defendant for the "honeycomb briquette heating stove" technology were concluded on the basis of equality and mutual benefit and through consensus, and their contents complied with relevant legal provisions. Since the Technology Contract Law of the PRC had already taken effect at the time the supplementary agreement was signed, and in accordance with Article 16 of that Law, which provides that "a technology contract, once lawfully established, is legally binding," the contract is a valid contract. Based on relevant evidence, during the performance of the contract, the plaintiff repeatedly went to the defendant's factory to guide production and assemble prototype stoves. On this basis, the plaintiff also guided the defendant in drawing new technical drawings, which were then developed into blueprints, and there were patent documents as a basis. These technical drawings and patent documents could all serve as standards for inspecting the technical quality of the product. After mastering the technology, the defendant's failure to mass-produce the "honeycomb briquette heating stove" was due to a shortage of raw materials and other reasons, not technical reasons. Therefore, the plaintiff fulfilled all his obligations under the contract, and the defendant's defense arguments were untenable. The defendant's failure to pay the monthly initial fees as stipulated in the contract constituted a breach. Pursuant to Article 24 of the Technology Contract Law, which provides that where the performance of a technology contract becomes unnecessary or impossible due to the other party's breach, one party has the right to notify the other party to rescind the contract, the plaintiff's reason for requesting rescission of the contract with the defendant was justified and should be supported. Pursuant to Article 41, paragraph 1 of the Technology Contract Law, since the defendant failed to pay the usage fees as stipulated in the contract, it should pay liquidated damages as stipulated in the contract. Accordingly, on June 30, 1988, the court rendered the following judgment:

1. The defendant, Kangda Automobile Decoration Factory, shall pay to the plaintiff, Liu Bingzheng, the monthly initial fees from May to November 1987, totaling 2,800 yuan;

2. The defendant, Kangda Automobile Decoration Factory, shall pay to the plaintiff, Liu Bingzheng, liquidated damages of 20,000 yuan;

3. The patent implementation license contract signed between the plaintiff and the defendant is rescinded;

4. The defendant's other claims are dismissed.

The total of items 1 and 2 above is 22,800 yuan, which the defendant shall pay to the plaintiff within 10 days after this judgment takes effect.

Court costs of 252 yuan shall be borne by the defendant.

After the first-instance judgment, the defendant, Kangda Automobile Decoration Factory, appealed to the Beijing High People's Court on the ground that "the plaintiff, Liu Bingzheng, breached the contract first by failing to provide technical drawings."

The Beijing High People's Court held at trial: During the performance of the contract, the appellee, Liu Bingzheng, brought the patent documents and technical drawings to the appellant, Kangda Automobile Decoration Factory, personally guided the implementation of the patented technology, guided the production of two prototype stoves, and guided the appellant in drawing new drawings, enabling the licensee to master the patented technology for producing honeycomb briquette heating stoves. Moreover, upon inquiry with relevant national standards authorities, it was determined that for an individual's technical invention, where conditions for producing blueprints are lacking, a detailed pencil drawing shall be deemed a formal drawing. The foregoing facts demonstrate that the appellee has fulfilled his obligations as stipulated in the contract. The appellant's grounds of appeal are untenable. The supplementary agreement signed by the parties on November 10, 1987, was concluded on the basis of equality and mutual benefit and through consensus. Although this agreement was not performed, it was established and is a valid agreement. The original judgment's decision to award the appellee the 1,600 yuan in monthly initial fees that Liu Bingzheng had voluntarily waived in the supplementary agreement was improper.

On May 25, 1989, the Beijing High People's Court, in accordance with Article 151, paragraph 1, subparagraphs 1 and 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC (for Trial Implementation), rendered the following judgment:

1. Items 2, 3, and 4 of the original judgment are affirmed;

2. Item 1 of the original judgment is reversed, and the appellant, Beijing Kangda Automobile Decoration Factory, is ordered to pay the appellee, Liu Bingzheng, monthly initial fees for three months totaling 1,200 yuan.

Court costs of 252 yuan for each instance shall be borne by Kangda Automobile Decoration Factory.
